title: Actionable MVP: Console dashboards & tracing cut with QA gates
creator: Lucia Morales
description: Goal: Reduce the initial Console observability surface to a tightly scoped, actionable MVP that delivers latency and cost visibility for production teams while deferring expensive features (full trace explorer, per-token billing breakdowns, long-term trace retention). This ticket captures the scope reductions, the specific acceptance criteria, the gated QA checks for rollout, and the follow-ups to backfill trimmed capability in future phases.
acceptance_criteria: Three dashboard cards implemented and visible in Console: (1) Model throughput (requests/sec) per model variant; (2) Latency P50/P95 per route and per model; (3) Aggregated cost by model (daily rollup) with top-5 cost contributors

Tracing is implemented as sampled spans with a lightweight explorer that supports single-request lookup by request-id and a timeline view limited to 30s windows; full trace flamegraphs and span-level search are deferred

Telemetry schema documented in Confluence and validated: events for request_start, request_end, cache_hit, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out; schema approved by Observability and Instrumentation leads
Backend endpoints for dashboard metrics emit stable, paginated JSON and are behind a feature flag (observability-lite) for staged rollout
Console UI follows the provided Figma mocks (link in links) and has accessible labels, time-range selector (last 1h/6h/24h/7d), and an export CSV button for each card
E2E smoke tests that assert metrics surface for synthetic traffic exist in CI and pass on feature-flag-on runs
Rollout plan (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> global) documented and runbook includes rollback if error rate or latency regressions exceed thresholds
Performance SLO: dashboard queries for 24h window must complete < 300ms P90 for common queries on dedicated infra during canary
QA gates: product sign-off, security review (if any PII touched), and SRE readiness check must be green before 50% rollout
decisions: Cut: Full interactive trace explorer and span-level search deferred to post-MVP (Q2). Rationale: high engineering/infra cost and low incremental value for first customers.
Cut: Per-token cost waterfall in the first pass. Keep aggregated daily cost by model and top spenders to enable immediate cost discussions.
Keep: Lightweight single-request trace lookup (by request-id) because it accelerates incident triage and integrates with existing incident tooling.
Implementation: Use existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus + Clickhouse rollup) for aggregated dashboards. Use sampled Jaeger traces stored for 72 hours for the lightweight lookup.
tradeoffs: User experience vs. engineering velocity: removing rich trace search reduces debuggability for complex performance regressions but speeds the initial delivery and lowers infra cost.
Data fidelity vs. cost: sampling traces and truncating retention means some incident investigations will need reproduction vs. having full retention which is expensive.
Rollout speed vs. risk: enabling the surface behind a feature flag allows safe iteration but slows immediate availability for all customers.
